visual: Compact, bushy flowering perennial producing masses of warm fiery orange to golden-yellow daisy-like flowers with prominent dark central cones, held above fresh green foliage through summer and into autumn.
water: Water regularly during establishment and during prolonged dry periods. Keep moderately moist but avoid persistent waterlogging.
soil: Moderately fertile, moist but well-drained loam, clay or sandy soil; adaptable across a broad soil pH range.
soilWarning: Avoid persistently waterlogged ground. Flowering and plant strength are reduced in excessive shade.
prune: Deadhead regularly to encourage continued flowering. Cut back old stems after flowering or leave seed heads over winter for wildlife and cut back in spring.
hardinessNote: Hardy through most of the UK, approximately -10 to -5°C. Good winter drainage improves reliability.
resilience: Robust and relatively easy to grow in a sunny position with adequate moisture.
uses: Sunny borders, prairie planting, wildlife gardens, cottage gardens, containers and cut-flower displays.
foliage: Herbaceous; fresh to mid-green leaves forming a bushy base beneath upright flowering stems.
container: Well suited to containers provided it receives full sun and regular watering.
uncertain: Exact Rudbeckia cultivar identity should be checked against the nursery label or breeder information; 'Fireball' is not sufficiently distinctive from the supplied label alone to confidently assign a species or hybrid group.
